text: Loop-closure consistency: A → B → A must look the same
description: Unsupervised spatial consistency (object permanence) along random camera loops, including translation loops.

status.comment: Prerequisite done: train.margin (36dddc2), a state margin simulated and observed like the app's OVERSCAN, losses and evaluate.py on the inner crop only. A/B 500 its from nice-net, margin 8 vs nodrop (evaluate.py 64 x 96, mean L1): holes push-pull 0.063 vs 0.184 (border disocclusions mostly vanish: content survives in the margin), net vs push-pull all pixels -14.5% vs -18.9%, holes +2.8% vs +12.1% (little left to fill). Note: margin also shifts the sampled crops, so baselines differ slightly (pp all 0.0727 vs 0.0763). The margin makes training closer to the runtime; use it for further runs (3.6 s/it vs 1.6 at 32+16 px). Next: the loop loss itself (replay the camera back to step 1, dt = 0, L1 against the step-1 prediction where both are covered).
